title: Sell Mineral Rights in Loyalhanna, PA
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Loyalhanna, PA
metaDescription: Loyalhanna, near Latrobe in Westmoreland County, sits near the Loyalhanna Dam and creek. Learn how flood-control land interacts with mineral rights.
heroLead: Loyalhanna sits along Loyalhanna Creek near Latrobe, in the shadow of the Loyalhanna Dam, where federal flood-control land and private mineral ownership sit side by side.
intro: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers built the Loyalhanna Dam for flood control decades ago, acquiring easements and, in some cases, full ownership of land along the creek. That federal involvement adds a wrinkle most Westmoreland County mineral questions don't have — before we can talk about your interest near Loyalhanna, we need to know whether your parcel is affected by a Corps easement or sits entirely on private ground.

sections.heading: Federal Easements vs. Private Mineral Ownership
paragraphs: An Army Corps flood-control easement typically restricts certain surface uses but doesn't necessarily extinguish private mineral ownership underneath. We check the specific easement language recorded against Loyalhanna-area parcels to understand what it does and doesn't affect before discussing value.

Even where a flood-control easement does apply, it typically addresses surface use and structures rather than eliminating private mineral ownership outright, so we always verify the exact scope before assuming a Loyalhanna parcel is off the table.

sections.heading: Wet-Gas Value Away From the Creek
paragraphs: Much of the mineral value in this area lies in the surrounding farmland and hillside acreage outside the immediate dam and floodway footprint, which sits inside Westmoreland's active wet-gas Marcellus window the same as anywhere else in the county.

sections.heading: What We Verify Before Any Offer
paragraphs: We confirm whether your parcel is inside the Corps' project boundary, pull the deed to see what minerals were reserved, and check for nearby unit or lease activity before putting together an honest range.

If your family has held Loyalhanna-area ground since before the dam project began, it's worth having the deed reviewed even if you've always assumed the Corps' involvement settled the mineral question one way or another.

faqs.question: Does the Loyalhanna Dam project affect my mineral ownership?
faqs.answer: It depends on whether your specific parcel falls inside the Corps' easement footprint — we check that directly rather than assuming.

faqs.question: Can drilling happen near a flood-control project?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific easement and setback requirements; we review that as part of evaluating your parcel.

faqs.question: Is the broader Loyalhanna area still part of active Marcellus development?
faqs.answer: Yes, it sits inside Westmoreland County's wet-gas window, and we check current unit filings for the specific area.

faqs.question: How do I know if my land is inside the Army Corps' project boundary?
faqs.answer: We check the recorded easement description against your parcel boundary at the Westmoreland County courthouse, which tells us definitively whether the Corps' footprint touches your land.
